en.setting: Palazzo Contarini faces the Grand Canal with a facade of pink stone, its carnival lanterns still burning as guests arrive by gondola. The mirror gallery on the piano nobile holds fourteen paintings, each with a provenance card, and a studio room on the third floor where a restorer's brushes are still wet. Venice wears its masks tonight, and behind them, a forgery operation six years in the making.
en.crime: Luca Marini, an art restorer, was found in the courtyard below the main balcony at dawn. His restoration notebook lay open beside him on the flagstones, and the stone railing above showed deep score marks where it had been deliberately weakened.

suspects.name: Countess Morvaine
suspects.intro: Owner of the palazzo and its collection, who received the inspector in the mirror gallery with her gloves on.

suspects.name: Carlo Bassi
suspects.intro: Arrived by gondola in a white silk mask, his invitation addressed to someone else and his glove torn at the palm.

suspects.name: Dr Klaus Winter
suspects.intro: Independent appraiser whose report on the Titian was due at the insurance office by Friday.

suspects.name: Elena Rizzoli
suspects.intro: Managed the exhibition schedule and private sales, her commission exceeding her annual salary.

suspects.name: Marco Dandolo
suspects.intro: Waited in the courtyard after midnight with a torn glove and no explanation for his presence.

suspects.name: Signora Pelosi
suspects.intro: Kept the palazzo keys and managed the household, having worked for the previous owners.

suspects.name: Inspector Bruno
suspects.intro: Cultural crimes division, arrived at dawn, having investigated the Countess once before in Milan.

es.setting: El Palazzo Contarini da al Gran Canal con una fachada de piedra rosa, sus farolillos de carnaval aun encendidos mientras los invitados llegan en gondola. La galeria de espejos en el piano nobile alberga catorce pinturas, cada una con tarjeta de procedencia, y un estudio en el tercer piso donde los pinceles de un restaurador aun estan humedos. Venecia lleva sus mascaras esta noche, y detras de ellas, una operacion de falsificacion de seis anos.
es.crime: Luca Marini, un restaurador de arte, fue encontrado en el patio debajo del balcon principal al amanecer. Su cuaderno de restauracion yacia abierto junto a el sobre las losas, y la balaustrada de piedra arriba mostraba profundas marcas de corte donde habia sido deliberadamente debilitada.

suspects.name: Condesa Morvaine
suspects.intro: Propietaria del palacio y su coleccion, que recibio al inspector en la galeria de espejos con los guantes puestos.

suspects.name: Carlo Bassi
suspects.intro: Llego en gondola con una mascara de seda blanca, su invitacion dirigida a otra persona y su guante rasgado en la palma.

suspects.name: Dr Klaus Winter
suspects.intro: Tasador independiente cuyo informe sobre el Ticiano debia entregarse en la oficina de seguros el viernes.

suspects.name: Elena Rizzoli
suspects.intro: Gestionaba el calendario de exposiciones y ventas privadas, su comision superando su salario anual.

suspects.name: Marco Dandolo
suspects.intro: Esperaba en el patio despues de medianoche con un guante rasgado y sin explicacion para su presencia.

suspects.name: Signora Pelosi
suspects.intro: Guardaba las llaves del palacio y gestionaba la casa, habiendo trabajado para los propietarios anteriores.

suspects.name: Inspector Bruno
suspects.intro: Division de crimenes culturales, llego al amanecer, habiendo investigado a la Condesa anteriormente en Milan.

fr.setting: Le Palazzo Contarini fait face au Grand Canal avec une facade de pierre rose, ses lanternes de carnaval encore allumees tandis que les invites arrivent en gondole. La galerie des miroirs au piano nobile abrite quatorze tableaux, chacun avec une fiche de provenance, et un atelier au troisieme etage ou les pinceaux d'un restaurateur sont encore humides. Venise porte ses masques ce soir, et derriere eux, une operation de faux de six ans.
fr.crime: Luca Marini, un restaurateur d'art, a ete retrouve dans la cour sous le balcon principal a l'aube. Son carnet de restauration etait ouvert a cote de lui sur les dalles, et la balustrade en pierre au-dessus montrait de profondes marques de ciseau la ou elle avait ete deliberement affaiblie.

suspects.name: Comtesse Morvaine
suspects.intro: Proprietaire du palais et de sa collection, qui a recu l'inspecteur dans la galerie des miroirs, gants aux mains.

suspects.name: Carlo Bassi
suspects.intro: Arrive en gondole portant un masque de soie blanche, son invitation adressee a quelqu'un d'autre et son gant dechire a la paume.

suspects.name: Dr Klaus Winter
suspects.intro: Expert independant dont le rapport sur le Titien devait etre remis au bureau d'assurance vendredi.

suspects.name: Elena Rizzoli
suspects.intro: Gerait le calendrier des expositions et les ventes privees, sa commission depassant son salaire annuel.

suspects.name: Marco Dandolo
suspects.intro: Attendait dans la cour apres minuit avec un gant dechire et sans explication pour sa presence.

suspects.name: Signora Pelosi
suspects.intro: Gardait les cles du palais et gerait la maison, ayant travaille pour les proprietaires precedents.

suspects.name: Inspecteur Bruno
suspects.intro: Division des crimes culturels, arrive a l'aube, ayant enquete sur la Comtesse une fois auparavant a Milan.

all_strong.en: Countess Morvaine had replaced fourteen paintings over six years, sold the originals through Zurich, and built her fortune on forgery as surely as the palazzo was built on water. When Luca Marini's restoration notes identified the fakes, she scored the balcony railing with a masonry chisel and waited for carnival to provide the crowd, the masks, and the darkness. The cadmium yellow in the Titian, the silk residue on the railing, the servants' stair bolted from inside, Marini's destroyed report — each reflection in the Venetian mirror showed the same face. The masks came off at midnight, and so did hers.
all_strong.es: La Condesa Morvaine habia reemplazado catorce pinturas en seis anos, vendido los originales a traves de Zurich, y construido su fortuna sobre la falsificacion tan seguramente como el palacio estaba construido sobre el agua. Cuando las notas de restauracion de Luca Marini identificaron las falsificaciones, ella marco la balaustrada del balcon con un cincel de albanileria y espero a que el carnaval proporcionara la multitud, las mascaras y la oscuridad. El amarillo de cadmio en el Ticiano, el residuo de seda en la balaustrada, la escalera de servicio cerrada desde dentro, el informe destruido de Marini — cada reflejo en el espejo veneciano mostraba la misma cara. Las mascaras cayeron a medianoche, y la suya tambien.
all_strong.fr: La Comtesse Morvaine avait remplace quatorze tableaux en six ans, vendu les originaux par Zurich et bati sa fortune sur le faux aussi surement que le palais etait bati sur l'eau. Quand les notes de restauration de Luca Marini ont identifie les contrefacons, elle a entaille la balustrade du balcon avec un ciseau de macon et attendu que le carnaval fournisse la foule, les masques et l'obscurite. Le jaune de cadmium dans le Titien, le residu de soie sur la balustrade, l'escalier de service verrouille de l'interieur, le rapport detruit de Marini — chaque reflet dans le miroir venitien montrait le meme visage. Les masques sont tombes a minuit, et le sien aussi.

who_strong_rest_weak.en: The Countess's name echoed through the palazzo corridors like footsteps on marble — unmistakable, but leaving no trace. The forgery operation was suspected, the financial motive clear, but the balcony railing told no story that a prosecutor could carve into a verdict. The scored stone could have been anyone's work, the silk fibre anyone's wrap, and the carnival masks had hidden every face that mattered. She was charged on the weight of her collection's deception, not the evidence of a single evening. Venice convicted her as it always has its frauds — slowly, elegantly, and without quite proving anything.
who_strong_rest_weak.es: El nombre de la Condesa resonaba por los pasillos del palacio como pasos sobre marmol — inconfundible, pero sin dejar rastro. Se sospechaba la operacion de falsificacion, el motivo financiero era claro, pero la balaustrada del balcon no contaba ninguna historia que un fiscal pudiera tallar en un veredicto. La piedra marcada pudo haber sido obra de cualquiera, la fibra de seda del chal de cualquiera, y las mascaras de carnaval habian ocultado cada rostro que importaba. Fue acusada por el peso del engano de su coleccion, no por las pruebas de una sola velada. Venecia la condeno como siempre ha condenado a sus falsificadores — lenta, elegantemente, y sin probar del todo nada.
who_strong_rest_weak.fr: Le nom de la Comtesse resonnait dans les couloirs du palais comme des pas sur le marbre — incontestable, mais ne laissant aucune trace. L'operation de faux etait soupconnee, le mobile financier clair, mais la balustrade du balcon ne racontait aucune histoire qu'un procureur puisse graver dans un verdict. La pierre entaillee aurait pu etre l'oeuvre de n'importe qui, la fibre de soie de n'importe quel chale, et les masques de carnaval avaient cache chaque visage qui comptait. Elle a ete inculpee sur le poids de la tromperie de sa collection, pas sur les preuves d'une seule soiree. Venise l'a condamnee comme elle a toujours condamne ses faussaires — lentement, elegamment, et sans tout a fait rien prouver.

wrong_accusation.en: The wrong guest was detained, and Countess Morvaine closed the palazzo gates behind the last gondola as if the carnival had simply run its course. The Zurich auction proceeded on schedule, the forged collection sold under crystal chandeliers, and Luca Marini's restoration notes disappeared from the studio desk before the cultural crimes division could catalogue them. The mirror gallery kept its fourteen paintings, each one a lie framed in gold, and Venice looked the other way — as it has done for centuries.
wrong_accusation.es: El invitado equivocado fue detenido, y la Condesa Morvaine cerro las puertas del palacio tras la ultima gondola como si el carnaval simplemente hubiera seguido su curso. La subasta de Zurich procedio segun lo programado, la coleccion falsificada se vendio bajo candelabros de cristal, y las notas de restauracion de Luca Marini desaparecieron del escritorio del estudio antes de que la division de crimenes culturales pudiera catalogarlas. La galeria de espejos conservo sus catorce pinturas, cada una una mentira enmarcada en oro, y Venecia miro hacia otro lado — como lo ha hecho durante siglos.
wrong_accusation.fr: Le mauvais invite a ete detenu, et la Comtesse Morvaine a ferme les portes du palais derriere la derniere gondole comme si le carnaval avait simplement suivi son cours. La vente aux encheres de Zurich a eu lieu comme prevu, la collection falsifiee s'est vendue sous des lustres de cristal, et les notes de restauration de Luca Marini ont disparu du bureau de l'atelier avant que la division des crimes culturels ne puisse les cataloguer. La galerie des miroirs a conserve ses quatorze tableaux, chacun un mensonge encadre d'or, et Venise a detourne le regard — comme elle le fait depuis des siecles.

cold_case.en: The carnival lanterns burned down to stubs and no one was charged. The palazzo was cleaned, the courtyard flagstones scrubbed, and Luca Marini's death was recorded as an accidental fall from a weakened railing. The insurance appraisal was quietly withdrawn, the Zurich auction postponed indefinitely, and the mirror gallery closed to visitors for the season. The fourteen paintings hung in their frames, each one reflecting nothing true, and the cracked mirror in the gallery went unrepaired — a single honest flaw in a room full of beautiful lies.
cold_case.es: Los farolillos de carnaval se consumieron y nadie fue acusado. El palacio fue limpiado, las losas del patio fregadas, y la muerte de Luca Marini fue registrada como una caida accidental desde una balaustrada debilitada. La tasacion del seguro fue retirada discretamente, la subasta de Zurich aplazada indefinidamente, y la galeria de espejos cerrada a visitantes por la temporada. Las catorce pinturas colgaban en sus marcos, cada una sin reflejar nada verdadero, y el espejo agrietado de la galeria quedo sin reparar — un unico defecto honesto en una sala llena de hermosas mentiras.
cold_case.fr: Les lanternes de carnaval se sont consumees et personne n'a ete inculpe. Le palais a ete nettoye, les dalles de la cour recurees, et la mort de Luca Marini a ete enregistree comme une chute accidentelle d'une balustrade affaiblie. L'expertise d'assurance a ete discretement retiree, la vente aux encheres de Zurich reportee indefiniment, et la galerie des miroirs fermee aux visiteurs pour la saison. Les quatorze tableaux pendaient dans leurs cadres, chacun ne refletant rien de vrai, et le miroir fissure de la galerie est reste non repare — un seul defaut honnete dans une salle pleine de beaux mensonges.

lucky_guess.en: The Countess was named because the palazzo was hers and the forgeries bore her ambition. It was ownership more than evidence, proximity more than proof. The scored railing could not be traced to her hand, the silk fibre was common to three guests, and the carnival had made witnesses of no one. She was convicted on the architecture of suspicion — a beautiful structure, like the palazzo itself, that looked solid from the canal but rested on nothing firmer than water and reputation.
lucky_guess.es: La Condesa fue nombrada porque el palacio era suyo y las falsificaciones llevaban su ambicion. Era posesion mas que evidencia, proximidad mas que prueba. La balaustrada marcada no pudo ser rastreada hasta su mano, la fibra de seda era comun a tres invitados, y el carnaval no habia hecho testigos de nadie. Fue condenada sobre la arquitectura de la sospecha — una estructura hermosa, como el propio palacio, que parecia solida desde el canal pero descansaba sobre nada mas firme que agua y reputacion.
lucky_guess.fr: La Comtesse a ete designee parce que le palais etait le sien et que les faux portaient son ambition. C'etait la possession plus que la preuve, la proximite plus que la demonstration. La balustrade entaillee n'a pu etre attribuee a sa main, la fibre de soie etait commune a trois invites, et le carnaval n'avait fait de temoin de personne. Elle a ete condamnee sur l'architecture du soupcon — une belle structure, comme le palais lui-meme, qui semblait solide depuis le canal mais reposait sur rien de plus ferme que l'eau et la reputation.

expressions.suspect:countess_morvaine: Countess Morvaine received the inspector in the mirror gallery with her gloves on. Her voice carried the cadence of someone accustomed to being believed.
expressions.event:balcony_fall: Luca Marini fell from the main balcony onto the courtyard flagstones. The railing showed score marks where the stone had been weakened.
expressions.motive:forgery_operation: Fourteen paintings in the Contarini collection had been replaced with forgeries over six years. The originals were sold privately through a dealer in Zurich.
expressions.suspect:carlo_bassi: Carlo Bassi arrived by gondola at half past nine wearing a white silk mask. His invitation was addressed to the previous owner of his seat.
expressions.suspect:dr_klaus_winter: Dr Klaus Winter examined the collection as an independent appraiser. His report on the Titian was due at the insurance office by Friday.
expressions.suspect:elena_rizzoli: Elena Rizzoli managed the palazzo's exhibition schedule and private sales. Her commission on the last three auctions exceeded her annual salary.
expressions.suspect:marco_dandolo: Marco Dandolo waited in the courtyard after the masks were removed at midnight. His glove was torn at the palm and he offered no explanation.
expressions.suspect:signora_pelosi: Signora Pelosi kept the palazzo keys and managed the household. She had worked for the Contarini family before the Countess acquired the property.
expressions.suspect:inspector_bruno: Inspector Bruno arrived from the cultural crimes division at dawn. He had investigated the Countess once before, in connection with a sale in Milan.
expressions.location:palazzo_contarini: Palazzo Contarini faces the Grand Canal with a facade of pink stone. The carnival lanterns still burned when the body was found at dawn.
expressions.location:main_balcony: The main balcony overlooks the courtyard from the second floor. The stone railing is original to the building and shows deep score marks at one joint.
expressions.location:mirror_gallery: The mirror gallery runs the length of the piano nobile between gilded frames. Fourteen paintings hang on the east wall, each with a provenance card.
expressions.location:canal_entrance: The canal entrance admits guests by water through an arched gate. A bronze key locks the gate from inside after the last gondola.
expressions.location:studio_room: The studio room on the third floor served as Marini's workspace during the restoration. His brushes were still wet when the room was sealed.
expressions.location:servants_stair: The servants' stair connects the kitchen to the upper floors without passing the gallery. The door at each landing bolts from the stair side.
expressions.location:courtyard: The courtyard is paved in Istrian stone and open to the sky. Marini's body lay at the base of the balcony, ten feet from the well.
expressions.location:private_salon: The private salon adjoins the gallery and is used for viewings. An auction catalogue lay open on the console beside two champagne glasses.
expressions.object:cracked_mirror: A mirror in the gallery shows a hairline crack running from corner to corner. The crack was not present in the previous season's photographs.
expressions.object:paint_analysis: A paint analysis of the Titian reveals cadmium yellow, a pigment not available before 1820. The painting is dated 1560.
expressions.object:forged_canvas: A canvas in the studio room matches the dimensions of the missing Bellini. The stretcher bars are new but the linen has been artificially aged.
expressions.object:balcony_railing: The balcony railing broke at a joint where the stone had been scored. The cut is straight and made with a masonry tool.
expressions.object:guest_list: The guest list for the carnival reception shows forty-two names. The Countess added three by hand after the invitations were printed.
expressions.object:provenance_file: The provenance file for each painting traces ownership to a private collection in Vienna. Two of the chains of ownership share a fictional dealer.
expressions.object:pigment_sample: A pigment scraping from the gallery Titian contains zinc white and synthetic ultramarine. Both substances postdate the supposed creation by three centuries.
expressions.object:silk_glove: A white silk glove was found on the balcony floor. The fabric matches the pair worn by Carlo Bassi at the reception.
expressions.object:auction_catalogue: The auction catalogue lists eight works from the Contarini collection. The estimated value of the lot exceeds four million euros.
expressions.object:restoration_notes: Marini's restoration notes describe inconsistencies in the paint layers of three works. His final entry reads not original, crossed out and rewritten.
expressions.object:canal_key: The bronze canal key was found in Signora Pelosi's apron pocket. The lock it opens was oiled recently and the mechanism turns without sound.
expressions.object:linen_fragment: A fragment of old linen was found in the studio waste bin. The weave matches a type manufactured in Belgium in the 1920s.
expressions.object:sale_receipt: A Zurich sale receipt records a Bellini purchased for over one million euros. The listed buyer is a known alias.
expressions.emotion:polished_grace: She poured coffee for the inspector without being asked. Her hand was steady and her posture did not shift when the forgeries were mentioned.
expressions.emotion:startled_poise: He set down his glass too quickly when the balcony was mentioned. The wine spilled and he wiped it with his glove.
expressions.emotion:measured_deflection: Each question about the paintings was answered with a reference to the provenance file. She never addressed the pigment analysis directly.
expressions.emotion:stiff_formality: Signora Pelosi stood with her hands clasped and answered in formal Italian. She addressed the Countess as 'la Contessa' even when speaking about the body.
expressions.emotion:avoided_subject: He changed the subject twice when the Zurich dealer was named. His notebook remained closed throughout the interview.
expressions.emotion:practised_dismay: She pressed a hand to her chest and said 'how terrible' in precisely measured tones. Her earrings did not swing.
expressions.modifier:railing_scored: The stone railing was scored along a horizontal line at the weakest joint. The cut reduced the load capacity to a fraction of its original strength.
expressions.modifier:modern_pigment: The pigment analysis found materials manufactured after 1900 in a painting attributed to the sixteenth century. The discrepancy is conclusive.
expressions.modifier:frame_swapped: The frame on the gallery Bellini does not match the catalogue photograph from three years ago. The gilding pattern differs at the lower left corner.
expressions.modifier:carnival_mask: Carnival masks were worn by all guests until midnight. After the unmasking, the balcony was accessible from the gallery stair.
expressions.modifier:door_bolted: The servants' stair door on the second floor was bolted from inside when checked at dawn. Someone used it and re-bolted it before leaving.
expressions.modifier:canvas_aged: The studio canvas had been treated with tea and varnish to simulate age. Under ultraviolet light, the treatment is clearly visible.
expressions.modifier:varnish_fresh: Fresh varnish was applied to two gallery paintings within the past month. The varnish conceals surface irregularities visible in earlier photographs.
expressions.modifier:scratch_on_stone: A scratch on the courtyard flagstone extends from the base of the balcony outward. The mark is consistent with a falling body striking stone.
expressions.modifier:glove_torn: The torn glove matches a pair sold by a single Venetian glovemaker. Carlo Bassi and Countess Morvaine both patronise this shop.
expressions.modifier:silk_residue: A trace of silk fibre was found on the balcony railing near the break point. The fibre matches the weave of the Countess's evening wrap.
expressions.action:canvas_switched: The original Bellini was removed from its frame and replaced with a copy. The switch was made in the studio room on the third floor.
expressions.action:railing_weakened: The balcony railing was scored with a masonry chisel along its weakest joint. The work required fewer than ten minutes.
expressions.action:studio_locked: The studio room was locked after the fall and the key was not found. Signora Pelosi stated she had not entered since the previous afternoon.
expressions.action:mask_removed: Masks were removed at midnight as is carnival custom. After the unmasking, guests moved freely between the gallery and the balcony.
expressions.action:notes_destroyed: Marini's final restoration report was removed from the studio desk. Only the working notes in his notebook survived.
expressions.action:sale_arranged: The sale of four paintings was arranged privately through a Zurich intermediary. The receipts were kept in a locked drawer in the private salon.
expressions.action:provenance_forged: The provenance documents for the replaced paintings were fabricated using aged paper and period-appropriate ink. One signature was traced from a genuine document.
expressions.action:stair_descended: Someone descended the servants' stair between midnight and one. The maid heard footsteps but saw no one when she checked the landing.
expressions.action:gallery_inspected: Dr Winter inspected the gallery collection during the reception interval. He requested a pigment sample from the Titian and was refused.
expressions.time:carnival_evening: The carnival reception began at nine and guests arrived by gondola. Masks were worn until midnight and the balcony was open from ten.
expressions.time:midnight_bell: The midnight bell marked the unmasking. By half past twelve the gallery was empty and only the Countess remained on the upper floor.
expressions.time:body_found_dawn: The palazzo maid found Marini's body in the courtyard at first light. The carnival lanterns had burned down to stubs.
expressions.time:gallery_closed: The gallery was closed to visitors at eleven for the private reception. The studio room was last accessed at half past ten.
expressions.time:auction_date: The auction was scheduled for the following month in Zurich. The catalogue had already been printed and distributed to collectors.
expressions.motive:collection_value: The forged collection was insured for twelve million euros. If the originals were discovered to be copies, the insurance claim would constitute fraud.
expressions.motive:exposure_risk: Marini's restoration notes identified the forgeries conclusively. His report to the conservation committee would have triggered an investigation.
expressions.motive:rival_claim: Signora Pelosi's late employer had disputed the Countess's purchase of the palazzo. The property claim was settled but the resentment remained.
expressions.motive:insurance_fraud: Elena Rizzoli stood to earn a commission on the Zurich auction. If the forgeries were exposed before the sale, she would face criminal charges.
expressions.motive:reputation_ruin: The Countess had built her social position on the collection. Exposure as a forger would end her standing in Venice and beyond.
expressions.witness:gondolier: The gondolier brought the last guest at half past eleven. He waited at the canal entrance until one and saw no one leave by water.
expressions.witness:palazzo_maid: The palazzo maid heard footsteps on the servants' stair after midnight. She found the courtyard door unbolted at dawn.
expressions.witness:night_guard: The night guard patrolled the courtyard at midnight and again at three. He did not look up at the balcony on either round.
expressions.witness:art_dealer: The art dealer from Zurich spoke with the Countess during the reception. He confirmed that four paintings were reserved for the spring auction.
expressions.witness:canal_boatman: A canal boatman saw a light in the studio window at half past one. The light went out after several minutes and did not return.
expressions.event:luca_marini_discovered: Luca Marini was found in the courtyard below the main balcony at dawn. His restoration notebook lay open beside him on the stone.
expressions.event:carnival_reception: The carnival reception drew forty guests to the piano nobile. Champagne was served and the gallery was open for a private viewing.
